data.name: Amihailu in Dreamland
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to a world of magic!


Amihailu in Dreamland is a magical, dreamy adventure starring Amihailu Dugashoba and her friends! In this game, you'll wander the echoey and endless halls and spooky painting worlds to solve the mystery and escape the fantasy world. Or you would solve the mystery, if anything Amihailu said made a grain of sense!

The game features light adventure and visual novel elements. Players will explore and solve the world's sparse puzzles and untangle the bizarre narrative in the surreal landscape of an alternate dimension.

reviews.review:
[b]My Playtime:[/b] 2.1h (finished the game)

[h1]Intro[/h1]
[b]Amihailu in Dreamland[/b] is an adventure game where you have to explore some bizarre locations to return home. It features a lot of beautifully designed locations that are accompanied by great soundtracks.

[b]Pros:[/b]
- Nice-looking visuals and music
- 2 endings

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Story is hard to follow
- You need to recheck all interactable objects to see if something changed regularly

[b]Specs[/b]
Intel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650

[h1]Should you play this game?[/h1]
[b]Yes.[/b]
[i]If you don't mind a lot of backtracking and rechecking previous objects to progress the game, try this game.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]In-Depth Review[/h1]

[h3]Visuals[/h3]
The visuals are the best part of the game. [b]Amihailu in Dreamland[/b]  takes place in several areas that stand out from the others. The parallax background gives a nice view of both the indoor windows and the outside, while the interiors help to give the bizarre feeling. Heck, I didn't even think that I played an [i]RPG Maker[/i] game during my playthrough at all - it was that good.

[h3]Story[/h3]
Sadly, the story is where the game falls through. I had an issue understanding the story, which might or might not happen because of the names. The full names of each character can be hard to memorize, so the game starts using nicknames for them. While the nicknames make them easier to remember, it was only used by the main character, making it hard to associate who is who. I even thought that they are two different people sometimes.

Regardless of the name issue, it still can be hard to understand the story. Sometimes, it feels as if the game throws a bunch of new facts without warning, and you have to accept it and proceed as it is. It can be hard to figure out what the characters want to do this way. To be honest, I still didn't know what the main character does near the end and how it even works.

[h3]The Game[/h3]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
Just like any other [i]RPG Maker[/i] adventure game, you are supposed to interact with a lot of objects to find some key items. These key items will then be used with other items to allow you to proceed. Some areas will be locked at the beginning, which will be unlocked as you progress through the game. This is where the gameplay feels repetitive, though. It doesn't tell which area is unlocked after an event, forcing you to backtrack and interact with every object that you couldn't interact with previously. The bad news is, there are a lot of these objects.

Moreover, some objects can't be interacted with unless you have a certain key item. It will usually tell you what sort of items you need and is easier to remember than in some locked rooms, although you still need to take some notes on it.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1947938720

As I said before, [b]Amihailu in Dreamland[/b] promotes a lot of areas. You'll be transported to different locations as you progress the game with newer objects and puzzles to finish. Despite having a lot of areas, you won't have trouble navigating to earlier locations. A lot of backtracking methods will be introduced to make it easier to do. Besides, the game will lock you out of some earlier areas once you have progressed further back in the game, reducing the need to waste your time backtracking and rechecking every object.

Puzzles are mostly in the form of using items with other items. Some puzzles require you to use some wits, but I found them to make no sense and used brute force instead. The instructions tend to not match with what I was supposed to do, making it almost impossible without that method.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1947938670

[b]Length and Replayability[/b]
The game has 2 endings. I obtained one ending in 1.8h and loaded my save to get the other ending in 3h (2.1h total). The game isn't difficult at all - it might feel repetitive since you need to backtrack and recheck some locked areas, though. As for replayability, you can replay the game to get the other ending, but you can always save before the branching point. Some optional actions are also locked as you progress, forcing you to replay the game if you want to see them. I myself played the game blind and missed some secrets, but I don't think it's worth another playthrough since I was tired of the backtracking.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
[b]Amihailu in Dreamland[/b] is an enjoyable game set in a bizarre world. Its story might be unclear, but it shines in its beautifully designed areas. That being said, it's not for everyone, especially with how repetitive the gameplay can be. If you are interested in beautiful-looking pixelated games, feel free to try this game - it's free, after all.
